item.text:
**Verdict:** Mostly no. Erdoğan’s 2024 record contains some real technocratic and rule-based counterexamples, but the dominant pattern is favoritism/clientelism through municipal takeovers, selective enforcement, media control, opaque property decisions, and tightly managed information.

| Side | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Erdoğan appoints technocrat Fatih Karahan to CBRT | Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye | 2024-02-04 | https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/en/tcmb%2Ben/main%2Bmenu/announcements/press%2Breleases/2024/ano2024-06 | Erdoğan replaced the departing central-bank governor with a professional economist and former Fed/New York Fed staffer, which is a real example of staffing a key institution with competence rather than obvious kinship or cronyism. | 7B.9; also 7B.5 |
| Positive | DMO says its system emphasizes transparency, competition, accountability, and digital e-tenders | Devlet Malzeme Ofisi Genel Müdürlüğü | 2024-05-03 | https://www.dmo.gov.tr/Eng/Home/EngIcerik/1212 | The state procurement agency describes a rule-based, digital procurement lane with competitive bidding and accountability norms, which is the strongest counterexample to a blanket patronage reading in procurement. | 7B.9; also 7B.5, 7B.7 |
| Positive | DMO Health Market expanded to most hospital demand and generated savings | Devlet Malzeme Ofisi Genel Müdürlüğü | 2024-10-17 | https://www.dmo.gov.tr/Home/Icerik/3992 | Centralized digital procurement covered most hospital drug and medical-supply needs and reported savings, supporting a technocratic service channel rather than a family- or clique-run one. | 7B.9; also 7B.5 |
| Positive | FATF says Türkiye made significant progress on AML/CFT reforms | FATF | 2024-06-28 | https://www.fatf-gafi.org/en/publications/High-risk-and-other-monitored-jurisdictions/increased-monitoring-june-2024.html | FATF credits Türkiye with progress on supervision, beneficial ownership, and financial intelligence use, which is relevant counterevidence to hidden-clientelism claims in the finance/ownership space. | 7B.9; also 7B.6 |
| Positive | IMF says Türkiye made legal and regulatory updates to improve AML/CFT | IMF | 2024-10-11 | https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/11/republic-of-trkiye-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-statement-by-556139 | The IMF says authorities updated AML/CFT rules and were preparing a new anti-corruption strategy, which is modest evidence of institutional pushback against opaque patronage. | 7B.9; also 7B.6 |
| Negative | Turkey unseats Kurdish mayors in crackdown after peace proposal | Reuters via ThePrint / Reuters | 2024-11-04 | https://theprint.in/world/turkey-unseats-kurdish-mayors-in-crackdown-after-peace-proposal/2341056/ | The government replaced pro-Kurdish mayors with administrators, showing central control over appointments and local authority rather than neutral merit or respect for electoral mandate. | 7B.9; also 7B.5, 7B.7, 7B.8 |
| Negative | Türkiye government removes elected opposition mayors | Human Rights Watch | 2024-11-07 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/11/07/turkiye-government-removes-elected-opposition-mayors | HRW says elected mayors were removed, councils dissolved, and trustees/appointees installed, which is direct evidence of clientelist, politically selective use of administrative power. | 7B.9; also 7B.5, 7B.7, 7B.8 |
| Negative | Turkey blocks access to Instagram platform but gives no reason | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-08-02 | https://theprint.in/world/turkey-blocks-access-to-instagram-platform-but-gives-no-reason/2204688/ | Nationwide blocking without explanation is a blunt information-control move, consistent with favoring the regime’s interests over open access and neutral public information. | 7B.9; also 7B.6, 7B.7, 7B.8 |
| Negative | Turkey’s 2024 Digital News Report | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey | The media environment remained tightly controlled, incumbents got disproportionate airtime, and critical outlets faced fines, which is strong evidence of favoritism in the information domain. | 7B.9; also 7B.6, 7B.7, 7B.8 |
| Negative | Shock and confusion as Turkey seizes earthquake survivors’ homes | Reuters | 2024-03-18 | https://www.reuters.com/commodities/shock-and-confusion-turkey-seizes-earthquake-survivors-homes-2024-03-18/ | Thousands of Hatay owners were blindsided by Treasury transfers under an urban-planning amendment with unclear compensation, suggesting opaque, discretionary, and politically fraught use of state power. | 7B.9; also 7B.7, 7B.8 |
| Negative | Turkey’s CB governor faces accusation of family influence on bank operations | Turkish Minute | 2024-01-18 | https://www.turkishminute.com/2024/01/18/turkeys-cb-governor-faces-accusation-of-family-influence-on-bank-operations/ | A formal complaint alleged the governor’s father influenced operations and personnel, which is not adjudicated proof but is directly relevant evidence of suspected family intrusion into a sensitive institution. | 7B.9; also 7B.5, 7B.7 |
| Negative | Erdogan ally floats Turkey constitutional amendment to let him extend his tenure | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-11-05 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/erdogan-ally-floats-turkey-constitutional-amendment-to-let-him-extend-his-tenure-3701715 | Erdoğan’s ally publicly floated changing constitutional rules to keep him in office longer, which is classic transactional power protection rather than non-favoritist governance. | 7B.9; also 7B.8 |

Search gap: I did not find strong 2024 evidence on pardons specifically, and I did not find a clean public record showing Erdoğan consistently avoided favoritism in all appointments or procurement. The clearest positive evidence is narrow and technocratic; the broader pattern remains political control and selective access.
